Build the **Email Templates** feature (card `cmsbkdmtc001fhlv5hekm984f`) for **Studio Nexis** (Next.js + Prisma/Postgres multi-tenant booking SaaS) at /opt/nexis on server **51.79.226.215**. Isolated branch; never disturb running prod/staging trees.

## Access & isolation (SAFE creds method — no plaintext)
SSH to .215 via the platform ssh2 approach (decrypt `server.rootPasswordEnc` for server id `cmsecmdps0001hlp27ai6mr7c`, pass straight into ssh2 without echoing; mirror lib/sftp.ts). ASSERT hostname/IP 51.79.226.215 first. Isolated worktree off prod HEAD:
`git -C /opt/nexis worktree add /opt/nexis-wt-email -b feature/email-templates origin/main` and build THERE with its own copied node_modules. If classifier-blocked, report what's left.

## Understand first
Current email setup: the one legacy "Verification code email" editor (around `settings/page.tsx`), the nodemailer/mailer mechanism, WHICH transactional emails the app actually sends today (booking confirmation, reminders, password reset, verification, receipts, gift-card if present, etc.), how templates/variables are stored, and the tenant `policies`/branding (logo) model.

## Build — proper email-templates area
- A dedicated **Email Templates** tab/section in admin: a LIST of every transactional email type the app sends, each editable.
- Per-template editing with **subject + body**, a **variable palette** (e.g. {{clientName}}, {{className}}, {{dateTime}}, {{studioName}}) that actually get substituted at send time, and a **live preview** rendered with sample data.
- **Defaults + reset**: every type has a sensible built-in default; a "Reset to default" per template. Unset templates fall back to the current/default copy so existing sends keep working.
- Include the **studio logo** in the rendered emails (use the tenant branding logo; the card notes the wizard didn't require a logo — surface/encourage it here).
- Keep it a clean, maintainable structure (store overrides in `policies` or a small `EmailTemplate` model — your call; if a model, additive Prisma only). Wire the send paths to use the tenant's template override when present, else the default.

## Rules
- Prisma changes additive only (I'll `prisma db push`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean + `npm run build` MUST pass in the worktree.
- Commit to `feature/email-templates`, push origin. Do NOT merge/deploy/restart.
- Board (Nxeon DB on /opt/nxeon): move card `cmsbkdmtc001fhlv5hekm984f` to In progress (`cmsbk8miq0017hlv5elhzx9vf`) + "Claude" comment. Clean up helper scripts.

Report: the list of email types made editable, how variable substitution + preview + reset work, whether you added a model or used policies, which send paths you wired to the templates, build/tsc status, and deploy steps.

import nodemailer from "nodemailer";
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { BASE_DOMAIN } from "@/lib/config";

// SMTP is optional. Without SMTP_HOST every send is recorded in EmailLog
// as "skipped" so the product behaves identically and flipping on real
// email later is just env vars + restart.
function transport() {
  if (!process.env.SMTP_HOST) return null;
  return nodemailer.createTransport({
    host: process.env.SMTP_HOST,
    port: Number(process.env.SMTP_PORT ?? 587),
    secure: process.env.SMTP_SECURE === "true",
    auth: process.env.SMTP_USER ? { user: process.env.SMTP_USER, pass: process.env.SMTP_PASS } : undefined,
  });
}

export async function sendEmail(opts: { tenantId: string; to: string; subject: string; body: string }) {
  const t = transport();
  let status = "skipped";
  if (t) {
    try {
      await t.sendMail({
        from: process.env.SMTP_FROM ?? `no-reply@${BASE_DOMAIN}`,
        to: opts.to,
        subject: opts.subject,
        text: opts.body,
      });
      status = "sent";
    } catch {
      status = "failed";
    }
  }
  await db.emailLog.create({ data: { ...opts, status } });
  return status;
}

export type EmailTemplate = { subject: string; body: string };

    ].join("\n"),

};

type Store = { emailTemplates?: Partial<Record<TemplateKey, EmailTemplate>> };

export function getTemplate(tenant: Pick<Tenant, "policies">, key: TemplateKey): EmailTemplate {
  const saved = ((tenant.policies ?? {}) as Store).emailTemplates?.[key];
  return { ...DEFAULT_TEMPLATES[key], ...(saved ?? {}) };
}

export function renderTemplate(tpl: EmailTemplate, vars: Record<string, string | number>): EmailTemplate {
  const fill = (s: string) => s.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (_, k) => (vars[k] !== undefined ? String(vars[k]) : ""));
  return { subject: fill(tpl.subject), body: fill(tpl.body) };
}

# rput.sh <localfile> <remotepath> — push a local file to the remote server

set -euo pipefail

B64=$(base64 -w0 "$LOCAL")
DIR=$(dirname "$REMOTE")
BYTES=$(wc -c < "$LOCAL")
CMD="mkdir -p '$DIR' && printf %s '$B64' | base64 -d > '$REMOTE' && echo \"WROTE $REMOTE $BYTES bytes\""
printf '%s' "$CMD" | (cd /opt/nxeon && node _rexec_helper.js -)

**Isolation confirmed.** Connected to 51.79.226.215 (hostname `nexis-app`) via the platform's ssh2 approach — decrypted `server.rootPasswordEnc` for server `cmsecmdps0001hlp27ai6mr7c` and passed it straight into ssh2, mirroring `lib/sftp.ts`. ### Email types made editable
I audited every send path (`grep sendEmail`) — the app only sends four transactional emails, all now editable in one place:
1. **Booking confirmation** (`public/book` on a successful book)
2. **Waitlist notification** (`public/book` when the class is full)
3. **Class reminder** (`cron/reminders`, 24h before start)
4. **Verification code / 2FA** (`login-verify`, previously the only templated one)

There is no password-reset/receipt/gift-card email in `main` today, so nothing else exists to wire.

### How it works
- **Variable substitution:** Each template declares its own variables. Booking/waitlist/reminder use `{{clientName}}`, `{{className}}`, `{{dateTime}}`, `{{studioName}}`, `{{manageUrl}}`; the code email keeps `{{studio}}/{{name}}/{{code}}/{{minutes}}` (preserves existing overrides). Send paths call a new `buildEmail(tenant, key, vars)` which merges the studio override over the default, runs `renderTemplate()` (regex `{{token}}` replace), and returns `{subject, body(text), html}`. I pass both `studio` and `studioName` aliases so either token works.
- **Live preview:** A client component (`src/components/settings/email-templates-editor.tsx`) renders the selected template with per-variable **sample data**, showing the exact branded email card (accent bar, logo header, body, footer) that recipients see, updating as you type.

- **Defaults + reset:** Every type has a built-in default in the registry. "Restore default text" repopulates the editor; "Reset to default" deletes the stored override (unset → falls back to default, so existing sends never break).
- **Logo:** Emails now render as branded HTML carrying `tenant.logoUrl` (resolved to an absolute URL) + `brandColor`.
